newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court approves ETA suspect's extradition.
newsitem.headline: French court approves ETA suspect's extradition.

text.p: The Paris appeals court gave a green light on Wednesday for the extradition to Spain of a suspected leader of the Basque separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), justice sources said.
Jose-Maria Arregui Erostarbe, also known as Fitti, 50, was detained in the spring of 1992 and is serving a 10-year term in jail in France for conspiracy and possession of weapons.

His lawyer Jon Gonzalez told Reuters that Spanish authorities believe he was an ETA expert on technical, electronics and weaponry matters. Erostarbe is suspected of sending booby-trapped parcels to ETA victims.
The extradition is subject to a possible appeal to the Supreme Court and to a decree signed by the French Prime Minister.
ETA members caught in France usually serve part of their French prison sentence before extradition.
ETA, battling the government in neighbouring Spain, have killed nearly 800 people in a drive for full Basque independence begun in 1968.
